gen-fs-new-title-gf-podkova: Podkova is bookish and traditional, its round c opening broadly like a doorway left ajar. New Title sits above it, bold and modern, with letters locked together like links in a fine chain.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-rhodium-libre: New Title leads with a bold, modern look, its lowercase stretching high and its letters linked like a fine chain. And Rhodium Libre follows in an editorial, traditional hand, brush ends lifting away before each curve closes.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-rokkitt: Rokkitt is the bookish one here, its c bent open like a paperclip and its lowercase sitting moderately high. New Title is the showier of the two, bold and modern, built for display with letters locked like chain links.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-sanchez: Dignified meets daring: Sanchez opens its c like calipers beneath a bold, chain-linked headline from New Title. New Title shows off; Sanchez settles in.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-solway: Authoritative is the mood Solway carries, with flat, stencil-like line weight and a generous opening into the e. Solway keeps a lengthy read steady and bookish, while New Title above it stands high, bold and linked like a chain.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-yuji-boku: Chain-link boldness up top, rod-like steadiness below: New Title takes a modern, high-lowercase stance while Yuji Boku draws each stroke like cable. New Title grabs attention; Yuji Boku stays dignified.
gen-fs-new-title-nunito-sans: Bold is the word for New Title, its high lowercase and chain-linked letters made for big, short lines. Nunito Sans stays soft underneath, with open-mouthed curves in its small letters.
gen-fs-nippo-fs-bespoke-slab: Nippo's small letters stand almost as tall as its capitals, drawn in a constant, marker-like line that looks cut from wire. Bespoke Slab, grounded and refined, is better for brief copy.
gen-fs-oswald-fs-trench-slab: Tightly knit and confident, Oswald packs its rows close with real muscle. Trench Slab counters with dignity, keeping a refined, minimal gap between lowercase and caps.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-eczar: Eczar reads in a traditional, literary voice, plain and unfussy across the line. Oswald does the heavy lifting up top with tightly knit, confident rows; Eczar keeps the words themselves quiet.
